# WO-001: "Good to know" tips and durable checklist ticks in the app
Status: open
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via tools/vendor.sh)
In-house reviewer on acceptance: wizard-packager (Nina Alvarez); qa-security if storage changes.

## Goal
The "Protect yourself" page in the desktop app (local dashboard) should match the website:
1. Show each checklist's `tips` (a list of short strings, field on `Checklist` in src/freemyid/models.py) under a "Good to know" heading, after the steps. Never show `notes` (internal research text).
2. Store and read checklist ticks through `src/freemyid/checklist_state.py` (already written and tested by the in-house team) instead of the event-replay code in `src/freemyid/wizard/protect.py`. Its functions have the same names and return shapes. Ticks written the old way must still show as ticked.
3. The per-site pages must ignore the reserved internal id `_checklist` the same way they skip `_consent`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- With fake data, a checklist that has tips shows a "Good to know" list with every tip; one without tips shows no heading.
- `notes` text never appears in any rendered page (add a test with a distinctive notes string).
- Ticking and unticking in the app, then reading via `checklist_state`, agree; an old untagged tick event still reads as done.
- Visiting the site page for `_checklist` does not show it as a broker (404 or skipped, matching `_consent`).
- Existing tests still pass: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_wizard_v03.py tests/test_checklist_state.py`; `ruff check` clean on changed files.
- Plain, calm wording for older non-technical users (docs/POSITIONING.md). Layout still fits 1024x768 at 150%.

## Allowed paths (the vendor may change ONLY these)
- src/freemyid/wizard/protect.py
- src/freemyid/wizard/views.py
- src/freemyid/wizard/ui.py
- src/freemyid/wizard/static/style.css
- tests/test_wizard_v03.py
- tests/test_wizard_protect_tips.py

## Out of scope / do not touch
Everything else, especially src/freemyid/checklist_state.py, models.py, storage/, server.py security behaviour (CSP, origin checks), and brokers/checklists.yaml content.

## Check-in plan
After the first session: the owner reads VENDOR_STATUS.md and the diff, then answers questions. Second check-in when the vendor reports done, then in-house review.
